rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer:
North American Aviation built the spacecraft Collins stayed in. That spacecraft was the command module Columbia.

Collins stayed in Columbia during the landing. [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

Columbia was Apollo 11's command module. [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Apollo 11's command module was Columbia (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The command and service module was built by North American Aviation. [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
The heaters ran on ground power for about eight hours before launch. The review board said the explosion started with an electrically started fire in the tank.

- **Ground power:** [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"
- **What the board said started it:** [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"
- **Switch rating:** [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"
- **Specification change:** [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"
- **Board's finding on the switches:** [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The notes don't explicitly say that the eight hours of 65-volt heater use is what damaged the switches. They state the voltage mismatch and the electrical fire separately.

rows.question: How long before Kennedy's speech at Rice University did NASA announce its Apollo mission mode?
rows.answer:
NASA announced the mission mode 63 days before Kennedy's Rice speech. That is 9 weeks, or about two months.

- NASA announced lunar orbit rendezvous as the Apollo mission mode on 1962-07-11. [[lunar-orbit-rendezvous]] "[stated] NASA announced it as the Apollo mission mode on 1962-07-11 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
- Kennedy gave the Rice University speech on 1962-09-12. [[john-f-kennedy]] "[stated] Gave the 'We choose to go to the Moon' speech at Rice University on 1962-09-12 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

The gap is 20 days left in July, 31 in August and 12 in September.

rows.question: Which Apollo 11 crew member earned a doctorate on the kind of rendezvous Apollo relied on, and in which year?
rows.answer:
Buzz Aldrin, the Apollo 11 lunar module pilot, earned the doctorate, and he earned it in 1963. [[buzz-aldrin]] "[stated] Earned an MIT doctorate in 1963 with a thesis on manned orbital rendezvous (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

Apollo's mission mode was lunar orbit rendezvous. [[lunar-orbit-rendezvous]] "[stated] NASA announced it as the Apollo mission mode on 1962-07-11 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

The notes link Aldrin to that mode with "studied lunar-orbit-rendezvous". His thesis is described only as being on manned orbital rendezvous. The notes never say it was specifically about lunar orbit rendezvous.

rows.question: The landing site described in the Apollo 11 Mission Report's powered-descent section was named by an astronaut. What was first about the Gemini flight he commanded, and when was it?
rows.answer:
The site is Tranquility Base, and Neil Armstrong named it. Armstrong commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, which was the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit.

- Armstrong named the site: [[tranquility-base]] "[stated] Named by Neil Armstrong at touchdown: Houston, Tranquility Base here, the Eagle has landed (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- His earlier Gemini flight: [[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] Earlier commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

The notes give only the year, 1966, and no more exact date. I dropped the claim that the powered-descent section covers Tranquility Base, because the only support in the notes is a link line, not a fact line.

rows.question: Before commanding Apollo 13, its commander flew on an earlier Apollo mission. Which photograph was taken on that mission, by whom, and on what date?
rows.answer:
The commander of Apollo 13 was Jim Lovell. He had already flown Apollo 8 in December 1968, the first crewed lunar orbit. [[jim-lovell]] "[stated] Flew Apollo 8 in December 1968, the first crewed lunar orbit (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

The photograph is Earthrise. Bill Anders took it on 1968-12-24. [[apollo-8]] "[stated] Bill Anders took the Earthrise photograph on 1968-12-24 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
Charlie Duke caught German measles, which started the swap. [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

Jack Swigert was brought in as a result. [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Apollo 13 role is prime command module pilot (was backup command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

Swigert later won a seat in the US House of Representatives. He was elected in 1982 but died before he could take office. [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:
The Apollo 11 crew member was Michael Collins. He was the command module pilot, and the command and service module is the kind of spacecraft that carried the tank.

- **The tank and the spacecraft:** The Apollo 13 tank was oxygen tank No. 2. The notes say its service module carried the oxygen tanks. [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
- **Who piloted it on Apollo 11:** [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **What he did during the landing:** [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: How many years separate Neil Armstrong's Gemini 8 command and John Young's command of the first Space Shuttle flight?
rows.answer:
The two commands were 15 years apart.

- Armstrong commanded Gemini 8 in 1966. [[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] Earlier commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"
- Young commanded STS-1, the first Space Shuttle flight, in 1981. [[john-young]] "[stated] Commanded STS-1 in 1981, the first Space Shuttle flight (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

1981 minus 1966 is 15.

rows.question: Which came first, Fred Haise's Space Shuttle Enterprise tests or Jack Swigert's election to the House of Representatives?
rows.answer:
Haise's Enterprise tests came first. They were in 1977, and Swigert's election to the House was in 1982.

- Haise "Flew the Space Shuttle Enterprise approach and landing tests in 1977 (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)" [[fred-haise]]
- Swigert "Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)" [[jack-swigert]]

rows.question: What did Margaret Hamilton and Wernher von Braun each lead?
rows.answer:
Margaret Hamilton led the software engineering division at the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory. That division developed the Apollo on-board flight software. [[margaret-hamilton]] "[stated] Led the software engineering division at the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory that developed Apollo on-board flight software (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

Wernher von Braun led the team that developed the Saturn V. [[wernher-von-braun]] "[stated] Led the team that developed the Saturn V (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

He was also the first director of NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center, from 1960 to 1970. [[wernher-von-braun]] "[stated] First director of NASA Marshall Space Flight Center, from 1960 to 1970 (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The fact lines start with a `[stated]` tag, which I left out of the quotes. I've put it back below.

The "mailbox" was an adapter for the CO2 scrubbers. It was made from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The crew built it from radioed instructions. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

It was needed because the two sets of canisters didn't match in shape. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes don't give any more detail on the build steps.

rows.question: List every Apollo mission in the brain that launched with a crew, with its launch date.
rows.answer:
Four Apollo missions in the brain launched with a crew. Apollo 1 does not count, because it never launched.

- **Apollo 8** launched on 1968-12-21 with Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders. [[apollo-8]] "[stated] Launched 1968-12-21 with Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
- **Apollo 11** launched on 1969-07-16. [[apollo-11]] "[stated] Launched 1969-07-16 from Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **Apollo 13** launched on 1970-04-11. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **Apollo 16** launched on 1972-04-16. [[apollo-16]] "[stated] Launched 1972-04-16 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

Apollo 1 was a cabin fire during a launch rehearsal on 1967-01-27 that killed three astronauts. [[apollo-1]] "[stated] A cabin fire during a launch rehearsal test on 1967-01-27 killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

The brain mentions Apollo 17 and Apollo 14 only in passing, with no launch dates. It describes Apollo 17 as the last crewed lunar mission. [[apollo-program]] "[stated] Apollo 17 in December 1972 was the last crewed lunar mission (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" It says only that Apollo 14 reached the Fra Mauro site in February 1971. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] The Fra Mauro landing site was later reached by Apollo 14 in February 1971 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" I left both out of the list above because the brain has no launch dates for them.

rows.question: Which people does the brain explicitly name as walking on the Moon?
rows.answer:
The brain explicitly names three people as walking on the Moon: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Charlie Duke.

- **Neil Armstrong:** he was the "First person to step onto the lunar surface on 1969-07-21 UTC (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[neil-armstrong]].
- **Buzz Aldrin:** he was the "Lunar module pilot of Apollo 11 and the second person to walk on the Moon (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[buzz-aldrin]].
- **Charlie Duke:** he "Walked on the Moon as Apollo 16 lunar module pilot (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)" [[charlie-duke]].

The brain says twelve astronauts walked on the Moon in total: "Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" [[apollo-program]]. It names only the three above as moonwalkers.

- **John Young:** he commanded Apollo 16, but no note says he walked on the Moon [[john-young]].
- **Michael Collins:** he stayed in lunar orbit aboard Columbia, so he did not walk on the Moon [[michael-collins]].

rows.question: Which companies and laboratories built Apollo hardware in the brain, and what did each build?
rows.answer:
Four organizations in the brain are recorded as building Apollo hardware:

- **Grumman** built the Apollo lunar module. [[grumman]] "[stated] Built the Apollo lunar module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
- **North American Aviation** was the prime contractor for the command and service module. [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
- **Beech Aircraft** was a subcontractor under North American. It built the service module oxygen tanks. [[beech-aircraft]] "[stated] Built the service module oxygen tanks under North American Aviation (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"
- **MIT Instrumentation Laboratory** designed the Apollo guidance and navigation system. [[mit-instrumentation-lab]] "[stated] Designed the Apollo guidance and navigation system (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" The notes also link it to building the Apollo Guidance Computer, but that link has no fact line behind it.

The North American note also links to Apollo 1 as something it built, again without a fact line.

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Dates the brain records for Apollo 13 in 1970, in order:

- **1970-04-06:** Physicals took place, and the blood tests from them showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided and announced. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". Jack Swigert replaced Mattingly as command module pilot. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The same day, Mission Control's abort decision changed the goal to a safe return. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-17:** The crew splashed down after using the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **June 1970 (no day given):** The Review Board report was published. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
